english.title: Fail to disclose offence - regulated sector - terrorism
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in the course of a business in the regulated sector,

(A)_[knowing or suspecting]_
(B)_[having reasonable grounds for knowing or suspecting]_

that another person has committed or attempted to commit an offence under

(C)_[section 15]_
(D)_[section 16]_
(E)_[section 17]_
(F)_[section 18]_
(G)_[**(..SPECIFY WHERE THE OFFENCE SPANS MORE THAN ONE SECTION..)]_

of the Terrorism Act 2000, failed to disclose that information or other matter to a constable or a nominated officer as soon as is practicable
english.legislation: Contrary to section 21A of the Terrorism Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) Subsection 21A(5) provides that a person does not commit an offence under this section if -
(a) he has a reasonable excuse for not disclosing the information or other matter;
(b) he is a professional legal adviser and the information or other matter came to him in privileged circumstances.

(ii) Subsection 21A(6) provides that in deciding whether a person committed an offence under this section the court must consider whether he followed any relevant guidance which was at the time concerned -
(a) issued by a supervisory authority or any other appropriate body,
(b) approved by the Treasury, and (c) published in a manner it approved as appropriate in its opinion to bring the guidance to the attention of persons likely to be affected by it.

(iii) This offence was inserted into the Terrorism Act 2000 by paragraph 5 of Schedule 2 to the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001.
(iv) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Attorney General is required before proceedings are instituted, see section 117.

other.powersofarrest:
Primarily consider: Arrest without warrant - terrorism
Also applicable: Arrest without warrant
other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
